text: Hoare called null his billion-dollar mistake. What is the deepest problem with it?
choices: It defeats the type system: every reference type is secretly itself-or-nothing and the compiler will not say which
explanation: When a method declares it returns a String, the type is supposed to be a promise. If it may return null, the promise is really 'a String, or nothing' and nothing tells you which. It also fails remotely, and it has no meaning of its own — not-found, not-initialized and error are indistinguishable.
